memory_update.text: POWL should remain in the Layer 1B universe for data-center electrical balance-of-plant because medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power systems map directly to AI campus power bottlenecks; verify repeatability of data-center orders versus lumpy mega-projects.

MOD should remain in the Layer 1B universe for data-center thermal balance-of-plant because filings explicitly link AI/HPC heat loads to high-density hybrid and liquid cooling demand, with fiscal 2027 Data Centers segment disclosure likely to improve tracking.
NVT should remain in the Layer 1B universe despite larger market cap because its liquid-cooling/CDU/manifold exposure and NVIDIA-related reference architecture create unusually direct node relevance.

Next Layer 1B pass should specifically search electrical contractors, commissioning firms, busway/cable tray suppliers, transformer specialists, and monitoring/software providers; IES Holdings and Atkore appeared as plausible but were not included due to the four-candidate limit.

node: Data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant: switchgear, transformers, busway, UPS, power distribution, cooling distribution units, cold plates, and monitoring
summary: Expanded the universe around the data-center electrical and thermal balance-of-plant node with one obvious reference anchor and three more focused second-order suppliers. The strongest underfollowed mappings are medium-voltage switchgear and packaged electrical systems, data-center thermal management including hybrid/liquid cooling, and liquid-cooling/power connection subsystems. Evidence is strongest where companies disclose data-center orders, backlog, capacity expansion, or AI/liquid-cooling product references. This is research support only, not a trading recommendation.
